A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ICPE research and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. The material can be matched across the added sections, renumbering, and layout changes without essential evidence gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on bandits, MNIST pixel sampling, binary search, Magic Room, and feedback graphs, including results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds a distribution-shift evaluation of ICPE in Appendix D.1.2 and Table 2.

M1.justification: The practical inference and Q-networks, losses, target updates, and stopping mechanism remain unchanged in Section 3.2 and Appendix C. Renaming ICPE to In-Context Pure Explorer and explicitly describing separate models for the two regimes clarify the implementation. New Algorithm 2 formalizes idealized training for theoretical analysis.

E1.justification: Appendix D.1.2 adds deployment under shifted environment distributions within the existing Gaussian-bandit family. The original bandit variants, MNIST, binary search, Magic Room, and feedback-graph tasks are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in the corresponding experiments, including TaS, TTPS, Uniform Sampling, I-DPT, DQN, I-IDS, DeepCMAB, and the feedback-graph baselines EXP3.G and Tas-FG. New Table 2 evaluates ICPE alone; the added citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The new shift experiment evaluates trained models using symmetric Dirichlet distributions with prescribed KL values of 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, and 4, for 4–14 arms, delta = 0.1, and horizon 100. This adds a testing protocol; the previously reported experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds a focused robustness analysis asking whether correctness and stopping time withstand changes in the bandit environment distribution (Appendix D.1.2, Table 2). Existing policy analyses, magic-chain examples, and MNIST adaptation and failure analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix D newly explains the seed/environment/trajectory hierarchy and its variance contributions through a random-effects model. This expands statistical documentation. Hierarchical bootstrapping, existing run counts, 95% confidence intervals, and MNIST chi-squared tests were already reported; no increase in runs is established.

E6.justification: New Table 2 adds correctness and stopping-time results for 36 combinations of KL divergence and arm count. For example, at 8 arms and KL = 4, correctness is 0.88 ± 0.01 and stopping time is 11.47 ± 0.28. Existing figures and tables retain their results, including tables renumbered after this addition.

T1.justification: New Appendix B.2 introduces an idealized fixed-budget training formulation, additional assumptions, and substantial proofs. Theorems B.14–B.15 bound policy suboptimality through Bellman residuals and separate approximation from finite-sample estimation error. The earlier optimality, certification, IDS, and sample-complexity results are retained, with later results renumbered.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the central claims: jointly learning acquisition and inference, transferring through context without parameter updates, and competitive performance without explicitly modeling information structure. The conclusion retains the contribution of learned task-adaptive search. Added theory and robustness evidence support this existing framing.

C2.justification: v3 interprets Table 2 as evidence of limited sensitivity to moderate distribution shifts. Section 5 expands applicability discussions to combinatorial hypotheses, simulator-based and offline-RL training possibilities, and the need for real-world validation. The separate appendix limitations discussion is retained.

D1.justification: v3 supplies an explicit code-repository address in the abstract and reproducibility statement, where v2 described code without a repository link. Section 3.2 also explicitly documents separate training for fixed-budget and fixed-confidence models. Existing architectures, hyperparameters, hardware, and software details remain.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds citations covering structured or constrained bandits, policy testing, and MDP identification. The new analysis cites Scherrer et al., Lazaric et al., and Györfi et al.; the conclusion adds application references. These extend the literature coverage while retaining the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 renames the ICPE expansion, updates the publication header and author footnote, corrects wording and references, and expands explanations of theoretical results, training regimes, uncertainty, and limitations. The overall section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the distribution-shift table and an idealized-training pseudocode display. Existing figures are retained, with changes in size, placement, and surrounding page layout; subsequent tables and algorithms are renumbered. There is no substantial redesign of the existing visual evidence.

improvement.justification: Appendix B.2 adds an explicit analysis of training approximation and sampling error, while Table 2 supplies targeted robustness evidence. Clearer training descriptions, statistical explanations, and repository access improve transparency. The gains are limited by the theory's idealized sampling and linear-approximation setting and the narrow scope of the added bandit-shift evaluation.
